# IITG Wi-Fi Network Intelligence — Model Card

**All data is synthetic**, generated by `generate_data.py` (project root) to represent
realistic *patterns* of campus Wi-Fi behavior. Nothing here should be
presented as an actual measurement of IITG's network.

## Target

`target_sustained_degradation_60m` — binary. A "sustained degradation
episode" is a run of ≥3 consecutive 10-minute observations with
`is_degraded == 1` (≥30 minutes). The target at time t is 1 if such an
episode begins or continues at any point in `(t, t+60min]`. See
`src/feature_engineering.py::build_target` for the exact implementation
and `src/feature_engineering.py::assert_no_leakage` for the automated
check that runs before every training run.

Positive rate: ~18.5% of rows.

## Features (93 total)

- **Current telemetry** (12 raw readings at time t): `connected_users`,
  `active_users`, `data_volume_MB`, `signal_strength_dBm`, `SNR_dB`,
  `channel_utilization_pct`, `interference_score`, `packet_loss_pct`,
  `latency_ms`, `jitter_ms`, `throughput_Mbps`, `AP_load_pct`.
- **Causal trailing features**, per metric in
  `{AP_load_pct, latency_ms, packet_loss_pct, channel_utilization_pct,
  throughput_Mbps, signal_strength_dBm, SNR_dB, interference_score}`:
  lag 10/20/30m, rolling mean 30/60m, rolling max 60m, rolling std 60m,
  and a rolling-slope trend proxy at 30/60m (`(s - s.shift(w))/w`,
  vectorized — a true per-window least-squares slope via
  `rolling().apply(polyfit)` was tried first and was too slow at 691K
  rows; this proxy captures the same "is it trending" signal).
- **Static**: `building_type`, `floor`, `AP_capacity`, `AP_age_months`.
- **Calendar**: `hour`, `day_of_week`, `is_weekend`, `semester_period`,
  `is_lecture_hour`, `is_event_active`.

## Excluded (leakage / hackathon artifacts)

| Column | Why excluded |
|---|---|
| `is_seeded_problem_location` | Generator ground truth; a real admin would never have this as a clean label |
| `demo_tag` | Names the exact locations rigged for the hackathon demo — pure leakage |
| `is_anomaly_injected` | Ground truth for evaluating the anomaly detector only, never a feature |
| `location_id`, `AP_id` (raw) | Kept only as grouping/join keys, never as model features |
| `network_quality_score`, `is_degraded` | Not leakage (both are current-timestep state), but not included by default — they're deterministic functions of the raw metrics already in the feature set, so including them adds collinearity without new information. Not yet run as an ablation experiment. |

All of the above verified programmatically before every training run via
`assert_no_leakage()`, not just documented in prose.

## Split

Chronological, never random. Default 120-day run:
- TRAIN: days 0–83 (Jan 5 – Mar 29)
- VAL: days 84–101 (Mar 30 – Apr 16)
- TEST: days 102–119 (Apr 17 – May 4)

Boundary buffer: the last 6 rows (60 min) per location are dropped from
the tail of TRAIN and VAL, so no row's forward-looking target window
reaches into the next split.

Event/exam regimes are distributed across all three splits (4 exam
blocks, 7 event days total) — an earlier version of the generator
concentrated both into single blocks that landed entirely in
TRAIN/never in VAL/TEST; this was found and fixed mid-project (see
Limitations).

## Model

XGBoost (`HistGradientBoostingClassifier` fallback if XGBoost is
unavailable), 300 estimators, max depth 5, `scale_pos_weight` set to
the train-set class ratio. Compared against: persistence, a fixed
`AP_load_pct > 75` threshold, a location×hour×weekday historical
lookup (fit on TRAIN only), and logistic regression on 8 raw features.

## Threshold

Selected on VALIDATION only: the lowest threshold clearing
precision ≥ 0.75, then maximizing recall among those — i.e. "catch
as much as possible without training admins to ignore the alert
feed." Frozen before touching TEST. Current value in
`models/threshold.json`.

## Headline Metrics (TEST, current data version)

| Model | Precision | Recall | F1 | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Historical baseline | 0.892 | 0.808 | 0.848 | 0.979 |
| GBM (frozen threshold) | 0.753 | 0.988 | 0.855 | 0.993 |

The GBM's real edge isn't the aggregate row — it's regime-specific:
recall 0.985 vs. 0.597 on event days, 0.979 vs. 0.406 at the
congestion-example location. See `reports/subgroup_metrics.csv` for
the full breakdown.

## Limitations

- Historical-baseline performance is partly an artifact of this
  generator producing repeatable day-to-day demand curves; real IITG
  traffic would likely show a *larger* GBM-over-baseline gap.
- The 60-minute sustained-degradation target is a congestion detector
  by construction. It will not and should not catch the
  infrastructure-example location's issues (zero sustained episodes
  there in TEST) — that's the diagnosis module's job, not this
  model's.
- Root-cause diagnosis: `OTHER_UNCERTAIN` sits at ~31% of degraded
  observations (down from ~46% after fixing two rule under-fire bugs
  found via testing — see `src/diagnosis.py` comments). The remaining
  uncertain cases are genuinely ambiguous (moderate load, healthy SNR,
  moderate interference — no single dominant driver), not a rule gap.
- A small residual false-positive mode exists in the diagnosis
  module: ~0.03% of cases get `WEAK_SIGNAL_INFRASTRUCTURE` from the
  relative-only branch at a healthy ~31 dB SNR (a normal location's
  ordinary low-percentile moment). Documented, not patched — flagged
  as low-priority given the rate.
- Lead-time figures are right-censored at 180 minutes (the lookback
  cap used when searching for how early a warning preceded an onset).

## What Should Be Done Next

1. Streamlit dashboard around these frozen artifacts (not yet built).
2. Consider an ablation run with `network_quality_score`/`is_degraded`
   included, to settle whether they add anything beyond collinearity.
3. Consider an ensemble (max of historical-score and GBM-score) to
   recover the ~362-row "historical caught, GBM missed" cases found in
   error analysis, without giving up the GBM's event-day advantage.
